newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims fell last week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims fell last week.

text.p: The number of Americans lining up for first-time unemployment benefits fell last week, the government said Thursday.
Filings for state jobless benefits stood at 336,000 in the week ended Nov. 30, down from a revised 344,000 in the previous week, the Labour Department said in its weekly report.
Claims in the week ended Nov. 23 were previously reported at 342,000.
The total number of Americans on jobless benefit rolls rose by 66,000 to nearly 2.47 million in the week ended Nov. 23, the latest period for which the data were available.
The latest figures were roughly in line with Wall Street's expectation that claims would drop to 337,000, with the week shortened by the Thanksgiving holiday.
The four-week moving average, which smooths out weekly fluctations, rose to 337,750.
The department said 13 states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Nov. 23, the latest period for which the data were available.
They included California, with 19,564; Texas, with 12,288; Minnesota, with 3,429; Oregon, with 3,175; North Carolina, with 2,427; and New York with 2,391.

California reported layoffs in the construction industry and in agriculture. Texas attributed its increase to the return to a five-day workweek after a shorter reporting period the previous week. Minnesota had layoffs in the construction industry and in manufacturing.
North Carolina reported layoffs in the service and transportation equipment industries, while New York had layoffs in the construction industry. Oregon gave no explanation for its increase.
Ohio was the only state reporting a decrease in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Nov. 23 week. It provided no reason for the drop of 1,725 in claims.
